reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in replacing point estimates of portfolio weights with expectations under a Bayesian posterior. The Bayesian Parametric Portfolio Policy (BPPP) introduces a prior on policy coefficients θ, which shrinks aggressive estimates toward zero. This is approximated using a Laplace method, assuming the posterior is unimodal and Gaussian. The resulting policy is an average over this posterior, effectively performing ridge-like shrinkage. In contrast, the standard Parametric Portfolio Policy (PPP) uses maximum likelihood estimation without regularization, leading to overfitting. The Laplace approximation allows for tractable computation while preserving Bayesian inference. The key insight is that in high-dimensional signal spaces, such as those involving 242 predictors, shrinkage improves generalization. The empirical gains—Sharpe ratio increase from 1.05 to 1.32 and turnover reduction from 9.54 to 6.03—validate this approach. The failure mode occurs when the posterior is multimodal or non-Gaussian, invalidating the Laplace assumption.
